revision_reason: Addressing plan reviewer feedback: (1) atomic branch lock + agent instructions, (2) warn-only mode for agent-role restrictions, (3) multi-PR delivery strategy. Also incorporates minor gaps: EGG_PHASE env var, refine/plan readonly deferral, feature flags.
title: Architecture: Enforce phase file restrictions via readonly mounts and commit-time validation
summary: This analysis defines the architecture for a four-layer defense-in-depth enforcement system that closes three gaps in the current phase restriction model: local modification bypass (Gap 1), unrestricted branch switching (Gap 2), and late enforcement wasting tokens (Gap 3). The revision addresses all three reviewer issues by: (1) co-locating the agent instructions update with the branch lock in PR-1 so they ship atomically, (2) specifying warn-only mode as the initial behavior for agent-role restriction wiring with a configuration flag for enforcement, and (3) splitting delivery into 3 independent PRs aligned with the risk assessment's REC1 recommendation.

architecture_decisions.title: Multi-PR delivery strategy with independent layers
architecture_decisions.decision: Split implementation into 3 independent PRs: PR-1 (L0 branch lock + L2 commit-time validation + agent instructions), PR-2 (L1 readonly mounts + EGG_PHASE env var), PR-3 (L4 post-agent auto-commit). Each PR can be merged, tested in production, and reverted independently.
architecture_decisions.rationale: The plan reviewer (Issue 3) and risk assessment R10/REC1 both recommend independent PRs per layer. A single PR spanning 9 files across 3 components creates a large blast radius and makes targeted revert impossible. L0+L2 are co-located because they both modify gateway.py git_execute() and share the same enforcement pipeline. Agent instructions must ship with L0 (reviewer Issue 1). L1 is independent (orchestrator/shared changes). L4 depends on L0's assigned_branch field but can be a separate PR.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Reviewer Issue 3: 8 existing files + 1 new file across 3 components. A bug in any layer would require reverting everything. Risk assessment R10 explicitly recommends against this.

L0 and L2 both modify gateway.py git_execute() in closely related ways. Separating them creates merge conflicts and duplicates the git_execute() modification work. 3 PRs captures the right granularity.

architecture_decisions.title: Atomic branch lock + agent instructions deployment
architecture_decisions.decision: The agent instructions update (mission.md, environment.md) MUST ship in the same PR as the branch lock code. The branch-lock-related instruction changes are included in PR-1 alongside the gateway enforcement code.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Reviewer Issue 1 (HIGH). Risk R2 identifies that current mission.md (line 52) explicitly tells agents 'To work on a different branch, use git checkout -b'. If the branch lock deploys without the instruction update, every running agent will hit the new enforcement and waste tokens. The risk assessment REC1 states this must be in the same PR.

remove: mission.md line 52: 'To work on a different branch, use git checkout -b <name> origin/<branch>'
mission.md line 72: 'WORKTREE WARNING: git checkout main FAILS. Always use: git checkout -b egg/<name> origin/main'
mission.md lines 73-74: 'Wrong branch fix: git log --oneline -1 (save hash), create correct branch, git cherry-pick <hash>'
environment.md line 44: 'git worktree add/remove: Unsupported — use git checkout -b instead'
add: Branch lock section: 'You are on a fixed branch for this session. Do not attempt to switch or create branches — these operations are blocked. Your branch name is available via git branch --show-current.'
File restore guidance: 'Use git checkout -- <file> to restore individual files from the current branch.'

Auto-commit note: 'When your session ends, any uncommitted changes to allowed files are automatically committed and pushed. You should still commit and push your own work as you go (for checkpoint tracking).'
Phase-specific guidance per phase (implement, refine/plan, PR) listing what the agent CAN and CANNOT modify

architecture_decisions.title: Warn-only mode for agent-role restriction wiring
architecture_decisions.decision: Wire check_agent_restrictions() into git_push() in warn-only mode initially. Add an EGG_AGENT_RESTRICTIONS_ENFORCE environment variable (default: false) to switch to enforcement mode after validation. In warn-only mode, log the restriction violation with full details but allow the push to proceed.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Reviewer Issue 2 (MEDIUM). Risk R6 identifies that check_agent_restrictions() is dead code that has never been enforced. Coder is blocked from tests/, test/, docs/. Tester is blocked from src/, lib/, docs/. These patterns may not reflect actual workflows. For example, a coder commonly needs to update test files alongside code changes. REC3 recommends warn-only for 1-2 weeks before enforcement to collect production data.

implementation.warn_behavior: Log audit event with role, blocked_files, and allowed_files. Return FileRestrictionResult.allow() so the push proceeds.
implementation.enforce_behavior: Current check_agent_restrictions() behavior — block the push and return error.
implementation.location: gateway/gateway.py git_push() handler, after the existing phase file restriction check

architecture_decisions.title: Branch-switching detection heuristic: conservative, fail-open
architecture_decisions.decision: Use a conservative heuristic that definitively blocks only clear branch-switching operations and fails open (allows + logs) for ambiguous cases. Block when: (a) branch-create flags detected (-b, -B, --create, --force-create), (b) git switch with a branch target (no -- separator). For git checkout without --, allow and log rather than guessing whether the argument is a branch or file.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Risk R3 identifies inherent ambiguity between branch names and file paths. False positives (blocking a valid file restore) are more damaging than false negatives (allowing a branch switch that will be caught at push time). The push-time enforcement remains as a safety net for false negatives.

ambiguous_allows_with_logging: git checkout <arg> (no --, no -b, could be branch or file — allow + warn log)
implementation.reason_no_subprocess: Risk R3 notes git rev-parse adds latency and has TOCTOU issues. Pure string parsing is sufficient for definite cases.

architecture_decisions.title: Implement-phase readonly mounts only; defer refine/plan whole-repo readonly
architecture_decisions.decision: For PR-2, implement readonly mounts only for the implement phase (4 specific .egg-state/ subdirectory mounts). Defer the refine/plan whole-repo-readonly approach to a future iteration after implement-phase mounts are proven in production.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Risk R9 identifies that whole-repo readonly for refine/plan phases may block agent tool operations (Claude Code writes files for analysis, git operations may need temp files). REC2 recommends deferring this. The implement-phase approach has much smaller blast radius — it only makes 4 specific .egg-state/ subdirectories readonly, leaving source code writable.
architecture_decisions.deferred_work: Refine/plan readonly-root mount requires integration testing with actual agent sessions before deployment. This should be a separate issue/PR after implement-phase mounts are validated.

architecture_decisions.title: EGG_PHASE as container environment variable
architecture_decisions.decision: Add EGG_PHASE to the container environment variables set during container spawn in container_spawner.py, alongside existing variables like EGG_PIPELINE_ID and EGG_AGENT_ROLE.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Reviewer minor gap. REC4 identifies that EGG_PHASE exists only on the Session dataclass (server-side) but is not set as a container environment variable. Agents cannot programmatically detect their phase. This is needed for: (1) .egg-readonly marker files to reference the phase, (2) agent tooling to explain restrictions in context, (3) agent instructions to provide phase-specific guidance. Include in PR-2 since it's co-located with the container_spawner.py mount changes.

implementation.location: Environment variable assembly (alongside EGG_PIPELINE_ID, EGG_AGENT_ROLE, EGG_ISSUE_NUMBER)
implementation.value: The phase parameter passed to spawn_agent_container()

architecture_decisions.title: Post-agent auto-commit routes push through gateway (keep session alive)
architecture_decisions.decision: Keep the gateway session alive until after auto-commit completes. The auto-commit script uses the session token to route its push through the gateway API, adding push-time phase validation as defense-in-depth. Session deletion occurs after auto-commit + checkpoint capture.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Risk R4 identifies that direct git push from the auto-commit bypasses all enforcement layers. REC5 recommends routing through the gateway. The ordering becomes: agent exits → auto-commit (with session still alive, push via gateway) → checkpoint capture → session deletion → worktree cleanup. This adds defense-in-depth at the cost of slightly more complex session lifecycle, but eliminates the only unvalidated push path.
cleanup_order: 2. auto_commit_allowed_changes(session) — commit + push via gateway API
